headline: ETFs lose $1.28B in a week, the most since June, while perp longs push funding up to 9.98%.
summary: Dollar spot money is still leaving: ETFs lost $1.28B over Nov 2–6, and the buyers stepping in are perp longs paying 9.98% funding, not new cash. Price has sat at the short-term holder cost of 75,867 for three days; loss-selling has not grown, buyers have not returned, and our selling-pressure gauge has hit 100. Watch Nov 10 CPI, the 75,000 bid wall and the estimated liquidation band below 73,800.

news.title: ETFs lost about $1.28B over Nov 2–6, the most since the week ending Jun 26, with Nov 4 the only inflow day; ether ETFs lost about $365M the same week
news.read: Our Nov 2–6 total (including the Nov 6 provisional) is −$1.282B, matching the report; two straight weeks of outflows. In the same week weighted funding rose from the 7% range to 9.98%: spot sells, perps buy (see today's finding). No change to the cycle view, but the ETF cost of 79,039 overhead is break-even supply.

news.title: After payrolls, CME FedWatch puts a 25 bp December hike at 76.8% (66.9% a week ago); 2-year yield 4.51%, 10-year 4.86%; CPI due Nov 10
news.read: Hike odds rose about 10 points in a week, part of why dollar money is not coming back. Our BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation is 0.751 and the real yield 2.60% (FRED Nov 5); a hot CPI on Nov 10 would push the odds higher. No change to the cycle view; Dec 4 payrolls come before the Dec 9 FOMC.

news.title: AI debt stress spreads into credit: CoreWeave 5-year CDS topped 1,289 bp, Nvidia CDS up 76% in a month to about 139 bp; Nasdaq down four weeks running, −3.4% this week
news.read: Tech selling has spread from stock prices into credit spreads and risk appetite is falling. BTC fell with stocks on Nov 5 but did not follow the rebound, so the link is stronger on the way down. Macro backdrop; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: Stablecoins shrank about $5.77B (−1.91%) over Oct 28–Nov 4, USDT about 63% of it; US bank reserves rose $67.57B over the same period
news.read: Matches our data: stablecoins $292.3B, −2.23% in 7 days and −$15.0B in 30 days (DefiLlama Nov 7), now below the $293B confirmation line of the Nov 3 finding. Overall dollar liquidity rose while the part flowing into crypto shrank, so the issue is appetite, not supply. No change to the cycle view.

news.title: US Q3 unit labor costs fell 0.7% annualized, productivity +3.6%, +2.4% year on year (BLS preliminary, Nov 5)
news.read: Strong hiring with falling unit labor costs means wages need not push inflation up, evidence against the hike case; markets still price about 77% for December. The effect on BTC hinges on Nov 10 CPI; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: The Labor Department's final rule on retirement-plan investments, covering alternatives including digital assets, went to White House review on Nov 5; FinCEN and the Fed withdrew the plan to cut the cross-border transfer reporting threshold from $3,000 to $250, effective Nov 9
news.read: The retirement rule is still under review and its final text is unknown; longer term it could open 401(k) access to ETFs. Withdrawing the threshold cut spares small cross-border transfers extra reporting. Both are slow structural items with no visible effect on near-term flows (ETFs −$1.28B in a week); no change to the cycle view.

findings.title: ETFs lose $1.28B in a week while perp longs pay up to nearly 10% funding
findings.lean_why: Spot buyers are pulling back and price is held by leveraged longs paying high funding; that leverage sits at the edge of the cost line, so a break would be amplified by liquidations.
findings.what: Dollar spot money is leaving while leverage moves in: ETFs had their worst week since June, yet perp longs keep paying more to stay long, two flows pointing opposite ways. ETFs −$1.28B over Nov 2–6, weighted funding 8.59% → 9.98% (The Block, Farside, SoSoValue, our data, Nov 6–7).
findings.why: ETF breakdown: of five sessions only Nov 4 saw an inflow ($74.6M); Nov 5 −$430.2M and Nov 6 provisional −$411.9M, the latter almost all IBIT (−$403M) while FBTC took in $42.8M (SoSoValue). Funding breakdown: OKX 10.01%, Hyperliquid 10.95%, Deribit 5.37%, weighted by open interest, so OKX and Hyperliquid are driving it. Cross-check: Coinbase premium 7-day −0.149%, stablecoins −2.23% in 7 days (DefiLlama Nov 7), Korea premium 7-day 0.60%, so spot is not absorbing anywhere; OKX spot taker delta was +815 BTC on Nov 7, one of the week's few buy days, OKX only. Contradiction: the Hyperliquid top 2,000 accounts are net short (13,243 vs 8,837 BTC), so the longs paying funding are smaller accounts.
findings.alt: The Nov 6 ETF figure is provisional and will be overwritten when The Block publishes. High funding can also come from fewer basis trades (long spot, short futures) letting the perp premium recover, not only new longs; funding settles every 8 hours or hourly and jumps around on thin weekends. Large Hyperliquid accounts may be market makers or hedgers, so this is not a whale bear call.
findings.history: Our weighted funding series only starts in May 2026, too short for a backtest. Sharp 7-day stablecoin drops (1-year 2% extreme) happened 4 times before, with a 30-day median of −2.8% afterward (baseline +1.7%); n=4, too few, background only.
findings.so: What changed is who holds price up: yesterday's 'bids and leverage' now leans more on leverage, with long funding up about 2.4 points in a week. What did not change is the location: price is still at the lower edge of the short-term holder cost of 75,867, and neither the market stage nor the exit framework moved. Conditional: a drop into 73,800–74,800 would trigger a batch of estimated long liquidations (estimate, OKX only), market sells that could speed a decline.
findings.next: By Nov 14: weighted funding at 12% or more while ETFs do not turn to inflows means leverage keeps replacing spot, confirm; the Coinbase premium 7-day average back above −0.05% means dollar spot is buying again, refute.

findings.title: 76K coins three days underwater: loss-selling not growing, buyers not back
findings.lean_why: Underwater short-term coins have not turned into real selling, which leans bullish; but spot buyers are absent and supply is thin from 66K to 74K, which leans bearish, so the two offset.
findings.what: Question: three days after price fell below the thickest short-term holder pile, is selling growing or drying up? Both sides are shrinking: no more people selling at a loss, and no new buyers either. Network realized loss $733M → $305M; short-term holders in profit 28.7% (Bitview, Nov 7).
findings.why: Cost map (CheckOnChain actual coin age, Nov 7): short-term holders 3.727M BTC at an average 75,200; thickest bands 76K (633K), 80K (537K), 62K (490K); the close of 75,754 is 1.6% below the 76K band. Two points in time (estimate, Oct 7 → Nov 6): new coins bought and unmoved sit mostly at 80K (526K) and 76K (428K); spent short-term coins came mostly from 84K and 82K; the estimate differs from actual by 3.5% in total with 8.6% misplaced. Behavior: short-term holder realized loss 4,299 → 4,177 BTC and profit 3,833 → 3,418 (CheckOnChain Nov 7), both lower; STH-SOPR 0.9914, a touch deeper than the Oct 30 low of 0.9918, a tiny gap. Buyers: ETFs −$412M on Nov 6, stablecoins −2.23% in 7 days, only OKX spot taker delta at +815 BTC. Contradiction: daily realized profit ÷ loss fell to 0.331, so a larger share of sellers are taking losses, just on smaller total volume.
findings.alt: Nov 7 was a Saturday with low on-chain and spot activity (volume 0.35× the 20-day average), so shrinking volume may just be the weekend, not seller exhaustion. Realized loss and STH-SOPR are per-UTXO, not entity-adjusted, so exchange wallet reshuffles get mixed in; CheckOnChain realized P/L is smoothed and about a day late. The 30-day turnover is an estimate.
findings.history: STH-SOPR dropped below 1 nine times in the past year, with a 30-day median of −0.6% afterward (baseline +0.6%), mixed direction. This dip low of 0.9914 is almost the same as Oct 30's 0.9918, tagged 'heavier' by a small margin; realized loss is 2.0 bp of market cap versus 13.2 at the Jun 30 low and 47.2 at the Feb 5 low (Bitview).
findings.so: Logic chain: the new 76K coins have been underwater for three days (A happened), but realized loss-selling shrank (B did not), so this is not capitulation; spot buyers have not returned (C did not), so price cannot get back above the 77,565 true market mean. Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 7): at a 74,000 close 2.612M short-term coins would be underwater, at 66,000 only 2.703M, and at 64,000 it jumps to 3.103M; there is no thick cost zone between 74K and 66K, and price tends to move fast through thin supply. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 14: short-term holder realized loss above 5,000 BTC means loss-selling is growing, refuting 'not growing'; a close back above the 77,600 true market mean means buyers are back, refuting 'not back'.

findings.title: Selling pressure maxed out; a bit less momentum away from the bottom combo
findings.lean_why: Past bottom combos did better than usual over 90 days but worse over 30 days and failed several times in early bear markets, so it cuts both ways.
findings.what: Our selling-pressure gauge has climbed since Oct 12 and hit 100 for the first time today (69 a week ago); momentum quality is 0.30, right at the 0.3 bottom-combo threshold (ours, daily closes only, Nov 7).
findings.why: Basis: not in signals; taken from chips.stress in the brief. Pressure accumulates each day momentum is below 0.45, and 21-day returns have stayed weak (−12.5% from the Sep 21 high), so it is maxed out; momentum 0.30 means a negative but not extreme 21-day t-value. Cross-check: STH-SOPR below 1 for two days (CheckOnChain) and 71.3% of short-term holders at a loss (Bitview) fit 'pressure built for a long time'; but network realized loss is only 2.0 bp of market cap versus 13.2 at the Jun 30 low, far weaker loss-taking than the last bottom.
findings.alt: It is a homemade close-only gauge with no on-chain input; a slow grind lower also fills it. The momentum threshold is a fixed parameter, so 0.30 versus 0.29 means nothing in substance. Weekend closes on thin volume are less representative.
findings.history: Since 2012 there were 21 bottom combos: up 30 days later 11 times, median +0.3% (usual 57%, +3.2%); up 90 days later 13 times, median +14.7% (usual 60%, +9.9%); 13 gains by the end of each combo, median +4.2%, with a median dip of 9.3% along the way. By era: 2012–2017 3 of 6, 2018–2022 6 of 9, 2023–2026 4 of 6; after April 2022 it fell another 51.5%, and both 2014 cases fell more than 40% further.
findings.so: What changed is the short-term position: price has been weak for a month, reaching what has often been a 'near bottom' reading. What did not: this is not a buy signal, and 30-day results have been worse than usual; market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 14: momentum quality below 0.3 forms the bottom combo, confirm; momentum quality back at 0.45 or higher stops the accumulation, refute.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: BTC about −10% from the September high, retesting the August breakout; STH supply in profit fell from ≥97.5% to about 38%; true market mean 77.7K, STH cost basis 75.7K, 200-day MA inside the 73–76K band, long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K; after the past three midterms BTC fell another 15–50% within 2–10 weeks. Conclusion: holding 73–76K is a healthy reset within the August uptrend; a break below 73K points to a longer consolidation.
